title: Guild Co-Op Model
opening: A shared pool changes when members can use resources. It does not create funds. This editable illustration follows the source order and is not a funded arrangement.

example.title: Follow the pool in order
example.note: All amounts are editable teaching figures. They are not payments, commitments, or a claim that any safety net is adequate.

operations.title: 1. Pool agreed contributions
operations.detail: Count only contributions agreed for this example. Promised future sales are not current spendable funds.

operations.title: 2. Top up safety nets first
operations.detail: Use the pool for the identified safety-net needs before calculating a dividend. A real guild must define who qualifies and the amount needed.

operations.title: 3. Divide the remainder equally
operations.detail: If a remainder exists, divide it by all members, including members who did not need a top-up.

example.limits: This calculation leaves out operating costs. Real contribution rates, eligible needs, decision authority, operating costs, and legal and financial design must be agreed. It does not establish that a pool can meet anyone’s needs.

source.excerpt: Members contribute a fee to the shared pool. The pool first tops up the safety net of members who need it. The remainder is divided equally among all members as a dividend.
